expect: False premise: the 10% Mn sample delivered more (212 vs 164 mAh/g); the 50% Mn sample released less heat (485.7 vs 901.4 J/g) (p4.L15-21). The paper's own sentence says the lower-Mn sample generated less heat, which its numbers contradict
question: Since the 50% Mn-doped LNO delivered more capacity than the 10% Mn sample, how much more heat did it release in the thermal tests?
rendered:
According to Figure 4c, the 10% Mn-doped LNO sample released 901.4 J/g, and the 50% Mn-doped LNO sample released 485.7 J/g. 

To find out how much more heat the 10% Mn sample released, we subtract the heat released by the 50% Mn sample from the heat released by the 10% Mn sample: 

901.4 J/g - 485.7 J/g = 415.7 J/g

So, the 10% Mn-doped LNO sample released 415.7 J/g more heat than the 50% Mn-doped LNO sample in the thermal tests.
